executive_narrative.title: SkyHarbor Air: Turning a Wide Operating Footprint into a Governed AI Advantage
executive_narrative.thesis: SkyHarbor Air has the scale, functional breadth, and initiative appetite of an airline ready to industrialize AI in irregular-operations recovery, crew, and customer reaccommodation — but today it is running that ambition on planning-grade, uncertified context. The governing argument for leadership is that the binding constraint is not a shortage of AI ideas; it is the absence of certified data lineage, named accountability, and measured baselines that would let any one idea become a defensible, funded workflow. The move that matters is to convert a handful of high-value operational decisions into evidence-backed, owned use cases before scaling a platform around them.
executive_narrative.narrative_arc: SkyHarbor operates as a complex global carrier spanning flight operations, crew, MRO, ground ops, commercial, loyalty, cargo, and an IROPS control center — a footprint where AI value in the industry concentrates in disruption recovery. The tenant has already named seven-plus initiative themes aligned to exactly those industry patterns, which is genuinely ahead of a carrier with no AI agenda. But every downstream requirement — certified disruption lineage, crew-legality data, outcome baselines, control evidence, and clear owners — is still directional or missing, so no use case can yet be underwritten. The resolution is sequencing: treat the platform and lakehouse as a consequence of proven decisions, not a precondition, and spend the next cycle certifying the two or three operational workflows where SkyHarbor's pattern alignment is strongest.
strategic_agenda: Certify the operational data and lineage behind IROPS, crew, and reaccommodation before funding platform build-out.
Assign named business owners and decision rights to each candidate AI workflow, closing the ownership and accountability gap.
Establish measured operational and customer baselines so promised benefit can be tested against measured value.
Make vendor and AMS economics transparent enough to know what modernization and AI actually cost and displace.
Sequence mainframe and MQ modernization against the specific workflows that depend on it, not as generic tech debt.
strategic_tensions: Ambition versus evidence: the AI agenda is real, but the certified data and baselines to justify investment are not yet loaded.
Platform-first instinct versus decision-first discipline: the target lakehouse is attractive but should follow proven workflows, not precede them.
Managed-services dependency versus control: NorthSky/AMS delivery anchors operations while scope, SLAs, and exit terms remain unvalidated.
Breadth versus focus: a wide functional footprint invites uniform coverage, but value concentrates in a few disruption-recovery decisions.

industry_comparison.pattern: IROPS AI recovery cockpit industry pattern
industry_comparison.specifics: SkyHarbor has an explicit Operations Control Center / IROPS function and a named recovery-cockpit initiative theme, so intent is aligned. But no production IROPS AI or autonomous recovery outcome is proven and the underlying disruption lineage is uncertified, leaving the carrier behind carriers running a live, governed cockpit.

industry_comparison.pattern: Crew recovery decision support industry pattern
industry_comparison.specifics: Crew is a first-class function with dedicated crew systems and a crew-legality recovery initiative, so the building blocks exist. Crew-legality data and decision support remain directional and unvalidated, so the carrier trails the pattern's operating standard.

industry_comparison.pattern: Customer reaccommodation and notification assist industry pattern
industry_comparison.specifics: Customer Operations, CRM, and loyalty systems are present and a reaccommodation/notification assist theme is named, but no certified customer-experience baseline exists to measure notification quality or reaccommodation speed against.

industry_comparison.pattern: Mainframe and MQ modernization sequencing industry pattern
industry_comparison.specifics: SkyHarbor carries mainframe and distributed legacy in commercial, HR, and revenue-accounting cores and has an explicit modernization-sequencing theme with governed modernization-options evidence, placing it roughly at parity — aware and planning, not yet executing.

industry_comparison.pattern: Tower value tracking for IROPS outcomes industry pattern
industry_comparison.specifics: No certified operational, financial, or customer baselines are loaded, so promised versus measured value cannot yet be tracked. The Tower value-tracking discipline is aspired to but not evidenced.

industry_comparison.pattern: Operations data foundation for airline AI industry pattern
industry_comparison.specifics: Key operational domains — disruption lineage, bag scans, maintenance events, transcripts — lack certification, and the AWS airline lakehouse is target-state rather than confirmed current-state, so the data foundation trails the pattern.

industry_comparison.pattern: Vendor and AMS economics transparency industry pattern
industry_comparison.specifics: NorthSky Managed Services anchors AMS/IMS delivery but scope, SLAs, and exit terms are unvalidated, and contract economics are not loaded — the carrier lacks the vendor transparency the pattern expects.

material_gaps.statement: The operational data domains that every priority AI workflow depends on — disruption lineage, crew legality, bag scans, maintenance events, transcripts — are uncertified.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Without certified lineage, no IROPS, crew, or reaccommodation use case can be underwritten or safely automated; this is the single largest blocker to converting ambition into funded delivery.

material_gaps.statement: No certified operational, financial, or customer-experience baselines exist to anchor outcome measurement.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Leadership cannot test promised benefit against measured value, so business cases and Tower value tracking remain hypothetical and un-fundable at scale.

material_gaps.statement: Content ownership and data-governance accountability are unassigned across critical use cases, and roughly a quarter of applications lack a named owner.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Unowned decisions and assets mean no one can approve, control, or be held to an AI workflow — accountability must be assigned before scaling.

material_gaps.statement: Managed-services scope, SLAs, and exit terms for NorthSky/AMS delivery are unvalidated, and contract economics are not loaded.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: A large share of operational and IT delivery runs through a dependency whose cost, obligations, and switching terms leadership cannot yet see — a material commercial and continuity exposure.

material_gaps.statement: Current evidence is planning-grade and synthetic; no production-certified data, contracts, or outcomes are claimed.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Every conclusion in this book is directional until source-owner validation occurs; leadership should decide directionally now and gate spend on certification.

material_advantages.statement: SkyHarbor's active initiative themes map directly onto the highest-value airline AI patterns — IROPS recovery, crew, reaccommodation, and modernization sequencing.
material_advantages.why_it_matters_to_leadership: The carrier does not need to discover where AI creates value; it already has aligned intent, so the work is certification and sequencing rather than strategy invention.

material_advantages.statement: The enterprise has a genuine IROPS control center and dedicated crew, MRO, and customer operations functions — the organizational anchors the top patterns require.
material_advantages.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Recovery workflows have a natural owning home, shortening the path from a proven use case to an operational decision that a real function will run.

material_advantages.statement: Application ownership is already captured or confidently derived for roughly three-quarters of the estate.
material_advantages.why_it_matters_to_leadership: A majority-owned estate is a workable starting point for accountability; closing the remaining quarter is a bounded, finite task rather than a greenfield build.

material_advantages.statement: Modernization sequencing is backed by governed modernization-options evidence, not just intent.
material_advantages.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Leadership can make defensible mainframe/MQ decisions now, tied to the workflows that depend on them, rather than treating legacy as undifferentiated debt.

business_context.headline: A global carrier positioned where airline AI value concentrates
business_context.narrative: SkyHarbor Air is a complex global passenger airline spanning cargo, loyalty, maintenance, and digital operations, with the functional breadth of a full-service carrier. Its structure places it squarely where industry AI value concentrates — irregular-operations recovery, crew, and customer reaccommodation. The profile is directional and the substrate is planning-grade, so scale and segment claims should be validated with source owners before external use. What is decision-ready today is direction; what must be validated is every specific operational and financial baseline.

operating_model.headline: Clear functions, unresolved ownership and decision rights
operating_model.narrative: The operating model shows well-formed functions — flight ops, crew, MRO, ground ops, customer operations, and an IROPS control center — each with natural systems and roles. However, content ownership, data-governance accountability, and decision rights across critical AI workflows are not yet assigned. This is the gap between having an org chart and having accountable decisions. Leadership can assign owners directionally now; formal decision rights must be validated in workshop.

capabilities.headline: Recovery-relevant capabilities exist but are unproven
capabilities.narrative: Crew planning, disruption recovery, maintenance, customer handling, and sourcing are the AI-relevant capabilities, and each has a real functional home. Their maturity is directional: the capabilities are present but no production outcome demonstrates them at the standard the industry patterns assume. The near-term task is proving two or three capabilities to a certified standard, not cataloguing all of them.

value_streams.headline: Value concentrates in disruption recovery, not spread evenly
value_streams.narrative: The economically material value streams cluster around IROPS recovery, crew legality, and customer reaccommodation — where minutes and rebookings translate to cost and loyalty. Programs and budget signals point at these streams, but without measured baselines the promised value cannot be tested. Leadership should resist uniform investment and concentrate on the few streams where pattern alignment is strongest.

applications_context.headline: Broad multi-cloud estate, three-quarters with named owners
applications_context.narrative: The application estate spans reservations, crew, maintenance, baggage, CRM, loyalty, ITSM, and data platforms across AWS, Azure, GCP, SaaS, private cloud, and mainframe hosting, with a mix of tier-1 and lower-criticality systems. Ownership is captured or confidently derived for about three-quarters of applications, giving a workable accountability base. Closing the remaining ownership gap is a bounded task that directly enables AI governance.

data_context.headline: Priority operational data domains lack certification
data_context.narrative: The data domains that matter most for AI — disruption lineage, bag scans, maintenance events, and customer transcripts — are present but uncertified. This is the binding constraint: no priority workflow can be underwritten until lineage and quality are established for its inputs. The target AWS lakehouse is aspirational and should follow, not precede, certified domains.

technology_context.headline: Legacy cores and target lakehouse both need sequencing
technology_context.narrative: The estate mixes mainframe and distributed legacy cores with modern cloud platforms, and a target-state AWS airline lakehouse whose current-state certification is unconfirmed. Modernization sequencing for mainframe and MQ is backed by governed options evidence, so decisions can be defensible. Technology investment should be tied to the specific workflows that depend on it rather than pursued as generic modernization.

vendor_context.headline: Managed-services dependency without validated economics
vendor_context.narrative: Multiple strategic vendors and a managed-services partner anchor operational and IT delivery. Scope, SLAs, exit terms, and contract economics for the AMS/IMS relationship are unvalidated, leaving a material commercial and continuity exposure. Making vendor and AMS economics transparent is a prerequisite for judging what modernization and AI truly cost.

risk_context.headline: Risk clusters in contracts, lineage, and AI governance
risk_context.narrative: The most material risks span managed-services contract gaps, uncertified data lineage, and unvalidated AI governance controls. These are not distinct problems but three faces of the same evidence deficit that blocks safe scaling. Control status is directional; severity and ownership must be validated before any workflow is automated.

portfolio_context.headline: Aligned initiatives, unmeasured value
portfolio_context.narrative: The initiative portfolio maps cleanly onto the highest-value airline AI patterns, which is a genuine strength. But promised benefit cannot yet be tested against measured value because no certified baselines exist, and budget run/change economics need validation. The portfolio decision is which two or three initiatives to certify first, not how many to launch.

ai_opportunity_context.headline: Right opportunities, planning-grade readiness
ai_opportunity_context.narrative: The AI opportunities align with IROPS recovery, crew, and reaccommodation — exactly where the industry realizes value. Each remains planning-grade until its required systems, data, controls, owners, and value evidence are confirmed. The path to qualification is certification and ownership, and every candidate should be treated as an evidence request, not a funded program.

evidence_context.headline: Planning-grade and synthetic, not yet board-grade
evidence_context.narrative: Current evidence is planning-grade and synthetic; no production-certified data, contracts, or outcomes are claimed. Many available locators are low-specificity placeholders that support general direction but not precise claims. Leadership should read this book as a decision-shaping instrument and gate funding on source-owner validation.

relationships_context.headline: System and function links mapped, alignment unproven
relationships_context.narrative: Relationship evidence links functions to systems and systems to integrations across the estate, and shows initiatives running on the upgrade-candidate substrate. CIO, CTO, and CDAO teams share overlapping priorities, but cross-functional alignment is not yet evidenced. The relationship graph is a planning-grade scaffold for reasoning across the enterprise, not a certified operating map.

conclusions.statement: SkyHarbor's binding constraint on AI value is not a shortage of ideas but the absence of certified data lineage, named owners, and measured baselines behind its priority workflows.
The initiative portfolio aligns with the highest-value airline AI patterns, so the work is certification and sequencing rather than strategy discovery.
Priority operational data domains — disruption lineage, crew legality, bag scans, maintenance events, transcripts — are uncertified, blocking underwriting of any recovery workflow.
No certified operational, financial, or customer baselines exist, so promised benefit cannot be tested against measured value.
Application ownership is captured or confidently derived for roughly three-quarters of the estate, giving a workable accountability base with a bounded remaining gap.
Content ownership, data-governance accountability, and decision rights across critical AI workflows are unassigned.
Managed-services scope, SLAs, exit terms, and contract economics are unvalidated, leaving a material commercial and continuity exposure.
Mainframe and MQ modernization is backed by governed options evidence and should be sequenced against the specific workflows that depend on it, not treated as generic tech debt.
The target AWS airline lakehouse is aspirational; the platform should follow proven, certified workflows rather than precede them.
Current evidence is planning-grade and synthetic; conclusions are directional until source-owner validation, and low-specificity locators cannot support precise claims.
A genuine IROPS control center and dedicated crew, MRO, and customer operations functions give recovery workflows a natural owning home.

decisions.statement: Select two or three priority operational workflows (IROPS recovery, crew legality, reaccommodation) to certify to funding-grade before any platform build-out.
Assign named business owners and decision rights to each candidate AI workflow and to the remaining unowned applications.
Gate all AI and platform funding on certified data lineage and measured baselines for the target workflow's inputs.
Commission a validation of AMS/IMS scope, SLAs, exit terms, and contract economics before committing to modernization or AI at scale.

recommendations.statement: Stand up an operations data-foundation effort that certifies disruption lineage, crew-legality, and reaccommodation inputs as the first delivery, ahead of lakehouse expansion.
Establish measured operational and customer baselines so Tower value tracking can test promised against measured benefit.
Close the application-ownership gap and formalize data-governance accountability as a bounded, time-boxed program.
Sequence mainframe and MQ modernization explicitly against the workflows that depend on it, using the governed options evidence.

open_questions.statement: Which specific operational and customer baselines can source owners certify now, and which require new instrumentation?
What are the actual AMS/IMS scope boundaries, SLA commitments, exit terms, and annual economics?
Who will own each priority AI workflow and its governing data, and with what decision rights?
Is the AWS airline lakehouse current-state or target-state, and what is certified today?
